title.narrative: African Swine Fever Compensation and Indemnization

description.narrative: In July 2021, APHIS confirmed the presence of African swine fever (ASF) in the Dominican Republic, near the border with Haiti. Epidemic outbreaks of ASF can result in significant economic impacts, depending on the duration of the outbreak, extent of trade embargoes, and reaction of producers and consumers to the disease and response measures. This agreement provided support for the control and eradication of ASF in the Dominican Republic, as requested by the Dominican Republic Ministry of Agriculture. This project (conducted in cooperation with IICA) provided funding for the provision of indemnity to producers for pigs that are depopulated or slaughtered to control the spread of the disease. APHIS determined that ASF is established in the Dominican Republic and reduced the amount available for the indemnity program in April 2024. APHIS is conducting an orderly drawdown of support as the Dominican Republic's program goal shifted from eradication to disease monitoring and surveillance.
